chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who had manumitted his slave partially (dabbara), then he needed the money for his price. He said: The slave is his. If he wishes, he sells him; if he wishes, he frees him completely; if he wishes, he keeps him until he dies. When the master dies, the slave becomes free from one-third of his estate.

key_terms.دَبَّرَ: To partially manumit a slave, setting a price for their remaining freedom

ai.seo_question: What are the legal options for a master who needs money after partially manumitting his slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the legal status of a *mudabbir* (a slave partially manumitted with the remainder due upon the master's death), affirming the master's discretionary right to sell, fully free, or retain the slave until his own death. It highlights the practical flexibility in Islamic inheritance law, where the outstanding manumission debt is settled from the one-third portion of the estate available for bequests, ensuring the slave's freedom is prioritized without disrupting the standard distribution of the remaining two-thirds among heirs.
